thread:
alexa: FYI onboarding quickstart failing for new users: Node SDK v1.15.0 sends camelCase keys and drops unknown flags, curl works. Spotted in sampleapp create-route step.

mohit: reproducible here. curl -> 201, SDK -> 400: server complains about unknown param traffic_percentage.

alexa: exact calls:
```bash
# curl (works)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes -d '{"name":"hello","traffic_percentage":30,"enable_rerank":true}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
```js
// node sdk (fails)
client.routes.create({ name: 'hello', trafficPercentage: 30, enableRerank: true })
```
SDK request shows {"name":"hello","trafficPercentage":30} -> enableRerank gone and key casing changed.

mohit: this is the typing filter we added; runtime drops keys not in the TS interfaces. Also the client normalizes keys to camelCase for JS ergonomics, which breaks server snake_case expectations.

tara: two pain points: 1) unknown experimental flags (enable_rerank) get filtered out, blocking quickstarts; 2) retry-on-auth-refresh can replay POSTs and create duplicates in Dedicated. curl doesn't retry so users see divergence.

mohit: short-term mitigation: preserve unknown top-level keys in a passthrough _raw object and log a one-line warning. Also stop auto-camelCasing on top-level request bodies for mutating endpoints until server-side compatibility window ends.

paul: and we should add an idempotency header generator for mutating ops to avoid duplicates on retries. If the user supplies their own Idempotency-Key, keep it.

sdk-bot: Created RDW-1420 - "node-sdk: param casing + unknown key stripping + unsafe retry on mutating ops" https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-1420 :white_check_mark:

paul: owners: @mohit do serializer passthrough + casing toggle, @tara add sampleapp CI test that posts an experimental flag and asserts server received it, i'll add idempotency header helper and a minor release note.

alexa: thanks all. small change but big impact for new users. will follow the patch release. :thumbsup:
